summary: "After 3.5 years of moving targets, llama.cpp v1.0.0 and ggml v1.0.0 freeze their public API with semantic versioning — and ship a llama-server hardening pass covering SSRF, DNS rebinding and CORS in the same breath."

Local inference has long had a version number that meant nothing. Every few weeks llama.cpp moved a function, renamed a parameter, or changed the shape of a context struct, and every downstream wrapper — desktop apps, agent frameworks, fine-tuning tools — absorbed the churn. The project that made running models on a laptop easy was, for a long time, the hardest dependency to pin.

**llama.cpp v1.0.0 and ggml v1.0.0 change that contract.** From this release forward, both libraries follow semantic versioning with an explicit rule set: breaking changes to the public C API are MAJOR, backward-compatible features and new model support are MINOR, and bug fixes with no API change are PATCH. API and ABI incompatibility now require a major-version bump, and the maintainers say plainly that they will be stricter about making those boundaries visible to downstream consumers.

**The release itself is a consolidation.** The deprecated public surface is gone: `llama_set_warmup` and 35 other deprecated functions were removed, along with the `defrag_thold` knob, and the NextN/speculative-decoding API was promoted out of the extension header into `llama.h`. New context parameters `moe_cache_size` and `moe_cache_cpu_share` let a host keep mixture-of-experts misses in system memory. OCP **FP8 KV caches** arrived via `-ctk`/`-ctv f8_e4m3`, with optional static per-tensor scales — the standard lever for squeezing a long-context model into a small memory budget. Three new text architectures landed (Kimi-K3.1-Pro, Ripple-65B-Preview, xing4_0), plus drama-3 TTS, MageVL-Cowork and Kimi-K3.1 vision support and external PLE shard loading. The library still spans **more than 150 architecture variants**.

**The security pass is the part worth reading carefully.** `llama-server` gained fixes for `--cors-origins` misconfiguration, DNS rebinding, and CORS-proxy SSRF, plus a fix for child-instance access. Two capabilities that were previously implicit are now explicit opt-ins: `--allow-unauthenticated-tools` and `--media-allow-private-urls`. MCP tool calls are now cancelled on client disconnect or timeout, and the `HF_TOKEN` is restricted to huggingface.co hosts. If you have ever exposed a llama-server beyond localhost, this release closes several paths you probably assumed were closed.

**Why it matters beyond llama.cpp.** The project counts on "a flexible but stable API" because downstream applications now depend on it by name. A 1.0 tag makes the library a legitimate pin in a release process — the same way people treat a stable compiler or kernel ABI. The ecosystem around local and private AI gets its first real guarantee that the ground will not move under it.

Release notes: [llama.cpp v1.0.0](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/releases/tag/v1.0.0) · announcement: [Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/blog/ggml-org/llama-cpp-v1)
